papers.title: Min-plus Bruhat decomposition
papers.abstract: We study min-plus Bruhat cells $B_{trop}^{(n)} \odot p\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}$, where $B_{trop}^{(n)}$ denotes the set of all upper-triangular matrices over $\RR \cup \{\infty\}$, and $p$ is a permutation. It is proved that $\dim (B_{trop}^{(n)} \odot p \odot B_{trop}^{(n)})= \frac{n(n+1)}{2} + l(p)$, where $l(p)$ is the length of $p$ in Coxeter generators. Also we provide an explicit description of the cell $B_{trop}^{(n)}(\RR) \odot p_0\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}(\RR)$ (up to a subset of dimension less than $n^2$) for the highest in Bruhat order permutation $p_0$. Finally, it is shown that for a tropically non-singular matrix $A$ for at most one permutation $p_A$ it can hold $A\in B_{trop}^{(n)}\odot p_A\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}$.

papers.title: The Iterated Local Transitivity Model for oriented graphs
papers.abstract:
Transitivity in social and other complex networks describes the tendency for two nodes with a common neighbor to become adjacent. We propose a new model for complex networks based on transitivity, called the Iterated Local Transitivity Model for Oriented Graphs (ILTO). The model generalizes the Iterated Local Model for Tournaments (ILMT). As in ILMT, oriented graphs are generated iteratively by cloning nodes and their adjacencies, with arcs between clones oriented either as the corresponding arcs between their parents or in the reverse direction. This process produces dense oriented graphs and, under suitable conditions, graphs with high connectivity and small diameter.
We analyze the universality properties of ILTO, showing that, for generating sequences with infinite support, the base oriented graph determines which oriented graphs appear as induced subgraphs, unlike in ILMT. We study motifs in ILTO and show that when the base graph is a tournament and the generating sequence has infinite support, the model generates quasirandom tournament sequences. Finally, we study domination numbers, the cop number, and the dichromatic number. We bound the cop number in terms of the independence number of the base graph and show that, for each fixed base graph, the dichromatic number is $\Theta(2^t)$ after $2t$ consecutive 0-steps.

papers.title: Remarks on the Farthing--Muhly--Yeend inverse semigroup of a finitely aligned higher-rank graph
papers.abstract: Given a finitely aligned higher-rank $k$-graph $\Lambda$, Farthing, Muhly and Yeend (Semigroup Forum 2005) constructed an inverse semigroup $S_\Lambda$ to provide a groupoid model for the $C^*$-algebra of $\Lambda$. In this paper, we extend some of the existing results related to the semigroup structure of a graph inverse semigroup to the more general setting of the inverse semigroup $S_\Lambda$. We obtain geometric descriptions of the Green's relations on $S_\Lambda$, which effectively generalize the existing characterization of Green's relations on a graph inverse semigroup. We provide a simple and useful description of the Cuntz-Krieger ideal of the Booleanization of $S_\Lambda$ and, based on this, identify a certain $X$-to-join Booleanization of $S_\Lambda$, where the abstract and concrete Cuntz-Krieger relations agree. Besides the natural partial order, $S_\Lambda$ is also ordered by set-inclusion. This helps us to realize $S_\Lambda$ as a semigroup \emph{graded-ordered} by $\mathbb{Z}^k$ and, subsequently, gives rise to a full inverse subsemigroup $S_\Lambda^h$ of $S_\Lambda$, which is graded by $\mathbb{Z}^k$ in the usual sense. We show that the Kumjian-Pask algebra of $\Lambda$ is graded isomorphic to the quotient of the contracted semigroup algebra of $S_\Lambda^h$ by the tight ideal. In the final part of the paper, we show that a $k$-graph morphism $p:\Lambda_1\longrightarrow \Lambda_2$ that is injective and satisfies a certain path lifting property induces, in a natural way, an injective $0$-preserving semigroup homomorphism from $S_{\Lambda_1}$ to $S_{\Lambda_2}$. In view of this, we build a suitable categorical setup to conclude that the isomorphism established between the Kumjian-Pask algebra of $\Lambda$ and the tight ideal quotient of the semigroup algebra of $S_\Lambda^h$ is natural.

papers.title: Short permutation pattern waves: The complete length-five classification
papers.abstract: For a permutation pi in Sk, a pi-wave is an increasing sequence of integers whose consecutive gaps have relative order pi. Let g(pi, n) be the maximum cardinality of a pi-wave-free subset of [n], and let P(pi, r) be the least integer N such that every r-coloring of [N] contains a monochromatic pi-wave. We determine the asymptotic orders of both functions for every permutation of length at most five. Existing upper bounds and weak-wave constructions provide sharp bounds for all but eight length-five patterns in S_5. For these eight exceptional alternating patterns, we establish g(pi, n) = Theta((log n)squared) and P(pi, r) = Theta(r(log r)squared).

papers.title: Circular flows and bisections of random regular graphs
papers.abstract: Jaeger conjectured that, for every positive integer $p$, every $4p$-edge-connected graph admits an orientation with congruent indegree and outdegree modulo $2p+1$. We prove a stronger probabilistic counterpart: a uniformly random simple $(4p+1)$-regular graph has a strongly connected orientation with all outdegrees in $\{p,3p+1\}$ with probability tending to one as its even order grows. More generally, for every fixed odd $d\ge9$, there is $\varepsilon_d>0$ such that its circular flow number is less than $2+4/(d-1)-\varepsilon_d$ with probability tending to one. We give explicit margins at the small degrees and prove the bound $91/33$ at degree seven, answering a fixed-upper-bound question of Li and Li. Gaps below $3$ at degree five and below $8/3$ at degree seven remain open. A uniform estimate for dense bisections also gives short intervals above the Li--Li maximum-bisection lower bound. Finally, we prove the one-unit bisection-gap conjecture of Greenhill, Isaev and Lewis: at every fixed degree $d\ge3$, the typical minimum parameter for orientations with outdegrees in $\{p,d-p\}$ exceeds the threshold forced by the maximum bisection by at most one.

papers.title: New lower bounds for kissing numbers in dimensions 32-35 and 37-39
papers.comments: 8 pages. Certificates and verification programs: this https URL (doi:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23527725) and this https URL (doi:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23554808)
papers.abstract: We show that the kissing numbers in dimensions 32, 33, 34, 35, 37, 38 and 39 are at least 352320, 370240, 390980, 415308, 499816, 605322 and 768916, improving the previous bounds 347584, 364736, 384836, 409676, 498024, 591900 and 763668. Except in dimension 38, the configurations are those of Edel, Rains and Sloane with new binary constant-weight codes of weight 8 and minimum distance 8 in the middle layer; each additional word adds 128 points. In dimension 38 we add 6855 antipodal pairs of vectors of the second shell of the Leech lattice to the empty equator of Kravatskiy's 591612-point configuration, where 144 pairs were known; this is an independent set problem in a regular graph of degree 11178 on 8386560 vertices. The codes and lines were found by local search, and all configurations were checked pair by pair in exact integer arithmetic.

papers.title: The nonexistence of nine-point crescent configurations
papers.abstract: A planar crescent configuration consists of $n$ points, no three collinear and no four concyclic, whose distinct distances have multiplicities $1,2,\ldots,n-1$. We prove by exact computation that no such configuration exists for $n=9$. The three pairs carrying the two least frequent distances yield a six-point subset with at most six distances. Rational linear algebra on quartic polynomials separates the possible six-point distance patterns into those with certified finite lists of normalized distance tuples and a residual family. Compatibility of overlapping subsets forces at least one core into the first family, without classifying the residual realizations. The remaining three points are then obtained by rational constructions over the field of the squared core distances. The multiplication matrices used to enumerate the core distances have order at most twelve. Exhaustive label assignments and exact algebraic comparisons exclude all remaining extensions.

papers.title: Good slopes, congruence preservation, and gaps over residue rings
papers.abstract: For $n\ge2$, a good slope of a permutation $f$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n=\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is an element $m\in\mathbb{Z}_n$ for which $x\mapsto f(x)+mx$ is a permutation. We call $f$ congruence-preserving if it preserves congruences modulo every divisor of $n$. For odd prime powers $n$, we classify all permutations with more than $n/2$ good slopes. Among permutations that are not congruence-preserving, we determine the maximum number of good slopes for $n=3^e$ with $e\ge2$, and for $n=25$, $125$ and $625$. Every permutation of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ has at most $\varphi(n)$ good slopes, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function. For several families of moduli with at least two distinct prime divisors, we prove a sharp upper bound for the number of good slopes of the permutations with fewer than $\varphi(n)$ good slopes. These families include $9q$ and $3q^e$ for every prime $q\ge5$ and every $e\ge1$. Together with a companion paper, this settles the bound for every odd composite modulus below $105$.

papers.title: Seshadri constants of singular loci of line arrangements with at most twelve lines
papers.abstract: Let ${\mathcal L}$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in the complex projective plane and let $Z={\operatorname{Sing}}({\mathcal L})$. A question of Pokora asks whether the multipoint Seshadri constant of ${\mathcal O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1)$ at $Z$ is always computed by a line of the arrangement containing the largest number of points of $Z$. We prove that the answer is affirmative for every arrangement of at most twelve lines. The proof uses a Bézout-type covering criterion, elementary restrictions on the intersection lattice, and a detailed analysis of the two extremal combinatorial types that can occur for twelve lines. One type is the Hesse arrangement; it is handled using a net of quartics through its twelve double points. The other type would yield a uniquely determined incidence structure on thirteen lines. We show that this incidence structure is not realizable over any field.

papers.title: The Lovász Local Lemma Is Sharp for the Hat Guessing Number
papers.abstract:
In the hat guessing game on a graph $G$, each vertex is occupied by a player wearing a hat whose color is chosen from a set of $q$ colors. Each player knows the graph and their position in it and sees only the hat colors of their neighbors. The players may agree on a strategy beforehand but must simultaneously try to guess their own hat colors without communicating. They win if at least one player guesses their own hat color correctly. The hat guessing number of $G$, denoted by $\textrm{HG}(G)$, is the largest integer $q$ for which the players have a strategy that guarantees a win for every assignment of hat colors.
A direct application of the symmetric Lovász Local Lemma shows that $\textrm{HG}(G) < e\Delta$ for every graph $G$ of maximum degree at most $\Delta \ge 1$. We prove that this bound is asymptotically sharp: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every sufficiently large $\Delta$, there exists a graph $G$ of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ with $\textrm{HG}(G) \ge (e - \varepsilon)\Delta$. This answers a question of Alon et al., disproves the conjecture $\textrm{HG}(G) \le 2\Delta(G)$ of Bosek et al., and improves on the construction of Latyshev and Kokhas, which achieves $\textrm{HG}(G) = 4\Delta(G)/3$. The hat guessing number thus provides a natural combinatorial problem in which the Lovász Local Lemma is asymptotically tight.

papers.title: Automatic partition identities
papers.abstract:
We encode certain sets of partitions by regular languages of boundary words, so that their generating functions become rational series in the quantum plane $RU=qUR$. An equality between two partition counts is certified by writing the difference of their series as $(1-U)a+b(1-R)$, with $a,b$ converging $q$-adically. We show that $a,b$ may be chosen as solutions of finite holonomic systems of $q$-difference equations computed from the automata, and describe finite certificates of their convergence, together with bounded searches for such certificates; the searches need not succeed, but a false identity is always detected.
As an application, we prove the three-row, level-two case of Primc's conjecture, which equates counts of coloured partitions subject to local multiplicity conditions with counts of coloured partitions whose parts lie in prescribed residue classes modulo eight.

papers.title: On Gallai $d$-colored circulants
papers.abstract: A $d$-graph is a complete graph whose edges are colored with colors from $[d]$. It is Gallai if it contains no triangle whose three edges have distinct colors. We prove that every Gallai $d$-circulant is an iterated lexicographic product of circulants using at most two colors. The proof uses the compatibility of the known canonical modular decomposition with the cyclic action. For $d$-graphs avoiding both a rainbow triangle $\Delta$ and the two-colored four-vertex graph $\Pi$ whose chromatic components are paths, we give a more explicit classification. Color-preserving vertex transitivity is equivalent to circular symmetry and to a reduced positional game tree whose branching numbers and labels depend only on depth. The edge colors in the given cyclic labeling are determined by a chain of divisors of the order. This description yields a complete isomorphism invariant and a linear-time recognition procedure in the difference-word representation. The characterization of CIS $d$-circulants reduces to CIS two-colored factors. Finally, we extend the numerical CIS criterion to $d$-graphs whose chromatic components are vertex-transitive.

papers.title: Optimal no-feedback card guessing after a fixed number of riffle shuffles
papers.abstract: An ordered deck of $n$ cards is subjected to $k$ independent Gilbert--Shannon--Reeds riffle shuffles. A player then guesses each card without feedback, with repeated guesses allowed. For every fixed $k\ge1$, we prove that, once $n$ is sufficiently large, an optimal guess at position $i$ in the top half of the deck is $\lfloor i/2^k\rfloor+1$; the bottom-half strategy is obtained by reflection. We also show that the optimal expected number of correct guesses is $2\sqrt{n/((2^k-1)\pi)}+O_k(1)$. Our starting point is the result of our earlier work that the label at each position is distributed as an equally weighted mixture of $2^k$ components, each a shifted sum of two independent binomial random variables (a Poisson-binomial distribution). The proof of the optimal strategy combines three ingredients: a uniform concentration estimate that separates the mixture components, exact binomial inequalities that control the gaps between competing peaks, and a coefficient comparison that resolves modal ties. The expected-score asymptotic is proved independently of the strategy, using only the peak heights of the mixture components.

papers.title: Almost Gorenstein edge rings of bipartite graphs and their $h$-vectors
papers.abstract: We characterize bipartite graphs whose edge rings are almost Gorenstein. Using this characterization, we recover known results for two families of graphs. In addition, we show that if the edge ring of a bipartite graph is almost Gorenstein and its $h$-polynomial has degree at least two, then the $h$-polynomial is palindromic except possibly for the linear and next-to-leading coefficients. Moreover, we construct two bipartite graphs whose edge rings have the same $h$-vector, although only one of the rings is almost Gorenstein.

papers.title: Binary Codes with a Forbidden Distance
papers.abstract: The maximum size of a t-intersecting code in the set of words of length n over an alphabet of size m, a problem posed by Frankl and Füredi, was determined independently by Ahlswede and Khachatrian and by Frankl and Tokushige. Extending this result to the forbidden-intersection setting, Keevash, Lifshitz, Long and Minzer proved that, for m greater than two and n sufficiently large in terms of t, (t minus one)-avoiding codes have the same maximum size and the same extremal ball constructions as t-intersecting codes. They also raised the binary case. Here, t-intersecting requires every two distinct words to agree in at least t coordinates, while (t minus one)-avoiding forbids agreement in exactly t minus one coordinates. We solve the binary case for all t at least three and n at least the square of the sum of t and one. If the forbidden Hamming distance n minus t plus one is odd, the maximum size of a (t minus one)-avoiding code strictly exceeds the maximum t-intersecting size. If it is even, the two maxima coincide, but their extremal families differ: some maximum (t minus one)-avoiding codes are not t-intersecting. We also determine all maximum avoiding codes in the even case. For odd forbidden distances, weight parity and a fixed-point-free pairing determine the maximum, while the diameter theorem gives the comparison with t-intersecting codes. For even forbidden distances, parity splitting and coordinate deletion reduce the problem to avoiding two consecutive distances. Connected components, disjoint neighbourhoods, and Harper's vertex-isoperimetric theorem yield the upper bound, which is attained by a t-intersecting construction. The diameter theorem then determines the extremal structure, and elementary binomial estimates give the stated parameter range.

papers.title: Testing Implies Distance Estimation with Polynomial Loss
papers.abstract:
A tester decides whether a graph has a property or is far from having it. A distance estimator asks for more: it must approximately determine how many edges need to be changed. A property is said to be testable if there is a tester with a number of queries bounded independently of the graph's order for each conceivable distance. Similarly, if a property admits an estimator with a number of queries bounded independently of the graph's order, it is said to be estimable.
Fischer and Newman proved that, in the dense graph model, every testable property is also estimable. We show that the passage from testing to estimation requires only a polynomial increase in query complexity. This resolves a long-standing open problem in property testing, previously tackled by Fiat and Ron, by Hoppen, Kohayakawa, Lang, Lefmann, and Stagni, and by Gishboliner, Kushnir, and Shapira.

papers.title: From MHV Gravity Amplitudes and Hodges map to Pentad Varieties
papers.abstract: We study some geometric aspects behind the Hodges matrix appearing in the context of scattering amplitudes for the $\mathcal N=8$ supergravity. Through a vector bundle construction, we show that the Hodges matrix gives rise to a canonical rational map from the two-step flag variety to symmetric matrices, called the $\textit{Hodges map}$. This construction allows to define the amplitude geometrically: its vanishing locus is a divisor - the $\textit{MHV gravity divisor}$. Inspired by the Hodges map, we introduce the notion of Hadamard ratio of two varieties. In the case relevant to gravity, this is the ratio of two Grassmannians, which we call the $\textit{pentad variety}$, connecting it to the pentad constraint from algebraic statistics. Moreover, we show that the pentad variety is closely related to the combinatorial algebraic geometry of Martin's affine slope variety, and the phirotopes of Below, Krummeck, and Richter-Gebert.

papers.title: Well-Covered Powers: Cartesian Products and Cayley Graphs
papers.abstract: We study graphs whose powers are well-covered, with an emphasis on Cartesian products and Cayley graphs. We first establish necessary conditions and sufficient criteria for Cartesian products, provide examples showing that a factor need not be well-covered and that two noncomplete factors can have the well-covered powers property, and classify several structured product families. In particular, we construct graphs satisfying the well-covered powers property for arbitrarily large diameters. We then show that the Cartesian square of a connected abelian Cayley graph is well-covered exactly when the graph is complete. We classify the well-covered-power graphs among connected circulant graphs of degree at most four. For Cartesian products of any number of complete graphs, we also prove that the recursive alphabet-size inequalities in the final conjecture are sufficient for all powers to be well-covered, prove partial converses for arbitrarily many factors, and give explicit obstructions for every binary prefix followed by one complete factor.

papers.title: Infinitely Many Almost-Uniform 3-Qualitative Independence Hypergraphs are Cores
papers.abstract: Qualitative independence is a property associated with the column vectors of well-known combinatorial designs known as covering arrays and qualitative independence hypergraphs characterize the existence of covering arrays on hypergraphs. The core of a hypergraph $H$ is an interesting structural characteristic to study, as it is the unique (up to isomorphism), minimal subhypergraph $H^\bullet \subseteq H$ which is homomorphically equivalent to $H$. We use the vertex transitivity and strong independence number of almost-uniform $3$-qualitative independence hypergraphs, $3\text{-}AUQI(2n+1,2)$, to show that $3\text{-}AUQI(2n+1,2)$ are cores for infinitely many $n$. Consequently, we establish that $3\text{-}QI(9,2)$ is a core and also obtain a lower bound on the strong chromatic number of $3$-qualitative independence hypergraphs $3\text{-}QI(2n+1,2)$.

papers.title: A King for Almost Everyone
papers.abstract:
A tournament is an orientation of a complete graph. A vertex $v$ controls a vertex $u\neq v$ if there is a directed path of length at most two from $v$ to $u$, and a $\delta$-king is one that controls at least $\delta(n-1)$ vertices. In the query complexity model, each query reveals the orientation of an edge. Shen, Sheng and Wu [SICOMP'03] established an $\Omega(n^{4/3})$ lower bound on the deterministic query complexity of finding a $1$-king, and a non-matching upper bound of $O(n^{3/2})$. Neither bound has been improved in over two decades, despite substantial progress on variants of the problem.
For $\delta$-kings with $\delta < 1$, Biswas, Jayapaul, Raman and Satti [Discrete Applied Mathematics'22] showed that $O(n^{4/3})$ queries suffice to find a $\frac12$-king. Lachish, Reidl and Trehan [FSTTCS'22] improved this guarantee to $\frac12+\frac{2}{17}$ using $\widetilde{O}(n^{4/3})$ queries, and asked whether a larger fraction could be achieved within the same query bound.
We answer this question affirmatively for every fixed fraction below one: for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, we give a deterministic algorithm that finds a $(1-\varepsilon)$-king using $O(n^{4/3})$ queries.
The design of our algorithm is informed by a structural analysis combining a sparse regularity lemma due to Allen, Kohayakawa, Mota and Parente [Electronic Journal of Combinatorics'14] with a new sampling argument based on a reachability theorem of Afek, Gafni and Linial [arXiv'19].

papers.title: Proper Conflict-Free Coloring on Structured Graph Classes: Bounds, Exact Algorithms, and Hardness
papers.abstract: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper vertex coloring in which every non-isolated vertex has a neighbor whose color appears exactly once in its open neighborhood. We study this coloring on chordal and ordered bipartite graph classes. For well-partitioned chordal graphs, we prove the tight bound $\omega(G)\leq\pcf(G)\leq\omega(G)+1$ and give an $O(n^2)$ construction from a partition tree. Every assignment of lists of at least $\omega(G)+1$ colors also admits a PCF coloring that respects the lists. Deciding whether $\omega(G)$ colors suffice is NP-complete, even when the partition tree is a star. This also proves NP-completeness on chordal graphs when the number of colors is part of the input. For interval graphs, we prove that lists of size $\omega(G)+1$ always suffice, improving the previous ordinary-coloring bound of $\omega(G)+2$. We use matchings to characterize when $\omega(G)$ colors suffice and give an endpoint algorithm taking $2^{O(\omega(G)^2)}n^{O(1)}$ time. We also characterize the exact value when the clique number is at most three and give a linear-time algorithm from sorted interval endpoints. For biconvex graphs, we prove a tight five-color bound and give a direct exact algorithm taking $O(n^{33})$ time. For bipartite permutation graphs, a smaller dynamic program gives an exact $O(n^{17})$ algorithm. Finally, if a bipartite graph is convex over an ordered shore $X$, we prove the sharp bound $\pcf(G)\leq\lceil\log_2(|X|+1)\rceil+3$ and construct a coloring in linear time from the order.

papers.title: Additive energy, Freiman's lemma, and an edge-isoperimetric problem on the boolean cube
papers.abstract:
Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite, non-empty set not contained in any translate of a hyperplane. We show that there exists a subset $S \subseteq A$ such that $d \ll |S| \ll d$ and
\[E(A,S) := |\{(a_1,a_2,s_1,s_2)\in A\times A\times S\times S:a_1+s_1=a_2+s_2\}|\ll\lvert A\rvert\lvert S\rvert.\] This can be interpreted as a robust, analytic generalisation of the classical Freiman's lemma, and recovers Freiman's lemma up to a constant multiplicative factor. In the process of proving this result, we also show that for any integer $1 \leq m \leq d$ and any set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $|A| \leq \binom{d}{m}$, one has \[ E(A, B) \leq 4(m + 1/m) |A||B|,\] where $B$ is the canonical basis of $\mathbb{Z}^d$. This gives new estimates for multiplicative energies between finite sets of primes and arbitrary subsets of positive integers, improving a previous result of Shkredov. Using related ideas, we also prove new bounds for an edge-isoperimetric problem for certain graphs on the boolean cube, improving an earlier result of Kirshner and Samorodnitsky. We give two different proofs of the first result described in this abstract and three different proofs of the second one.

papers.title: Resolvent comparison for Hermitian block matrices and Kelmans transformations
papers.abstract: A Kelmans transformation increases or preserves the largest eigenvalue of a symmetric nonnegative matrix. We determine when this comparison holds for Hermitian block extensions with a fixed coupling and an arbitrary common complementary block. An orthogonal change of basis and Schur complementation give an exact formula for the compressed resolvent difference as a difference of two rank-one matrices. This formula characterizes admissible coupling subspaces by proportionality of projected resolvent vectors. Polynomial coefficient kernels describe all such subspaces, and cyclic subspaces give dimension bounds and a maximum-dimension result for a two-block family. We also prove a general block comparison theorem and give monotonicity and equality criteria for nonnegative rank-one couplings. Applications concern graph joins, complex attachments, and Hermitian adjacency matrices.

papers.title: On the lower- and upper bounds of three-colored anti-Ramsey numbers
papers.abstract: In this paper we study a relatively new Ramsey type graph parameter introduced by my Bachelor's thesis supervisor Nóra Almási, and her Master's thesis supervisor Maria Axenovich. The parameter $\xi(G)$ denotes the largest natural number $n$, such that there is a red-blue-green edge coloring of $K_n$, such that in the edge coloring all copies of $G$ represent all three colors. After a brief recap on Ramsey numbers, we precisely define $\xi(G)$, and take a look at its relations to the Ramsey numbers. In the third chapter we establish lower bounds on $\xi(G)$, in the cases $G=K_5$ and $G=K_6$, namely $\xi(K_5)\ge 19$ and $\xi(K_6)\ge 31$.

papers.title: Co-Decompositions and FO Model Checking
papers.abstract:
Tree decompositions describe large graphs as gluings of smaller component parts. Here we study their categorical duals, tree co-decompositions, which construct large graphs via fibered products of small constituent parts. Co-decompositions are compressed representations of graphs or relational structures: the decomposed object can be exponentially larger than the space required to specify the co-decomposition.
Our main contribution is an algorithmic meta-theorem for first order logic: given only a co-decomposition of a $\sigma$-structure $G$ with $b$ bags, each of size at most $w$ and an FO sentence $\phi$, there is an algorithm which, without ever constructing or inspecting $G$, operates on the co-decomposition and determines whether $G \models \phi$ in time $f_\sigma(w,|\varphi|)\cdot b$. We pair this algorithm with structural results on tree co-width, including its relationship to tree-width and a separation from twin-width. Furthermore, we characterize bounded path co-width using a graph grammar. In contrast to our logical meta-theorem, we prove that $(s,t)$-Path becomes NP-hard on co-decomposition inputs. These results demonstrate how categorical constructions can enable efficient computation on exponentially compressed structures.

papers.title: Polynomial configurations and pointwise averages along Piatetski--Shapiro primes
papers.comments: 15 pages. An AI-assisted Lean development formalizes the deductions in the paper, conditional on eight explicitly documented families of external results. The development is available at this https URL
papers.abstract: For every \(c>1\) sufficiently close to \(1\), we prove that there is \(\kappa>0\) such that every sufficiently large \(A\subset[N]\) of density at least \((\log N)^{-\kappa}\) contains \[ x,\ x+(p-1),\ x+(p-1)^2,\ldots,\ x+(p-1)^k, \qquad p=\lfloor n^c\rfloor\in\mathbb P. \] We also prove pointwise almost-everywhere convergence of the corresponding multiple ergodic averages.

papers.title: Online packing of the three largest trees
papers.abstract:
For every $n\ge4$, arbitrary trees of orders $n,n-1,n-2$ can be packed into $K_n$ online, in decreasing order of size: each tree must be embedded before the next is revealed, and earlier embeddings cannot be changed. This strengthens the classical three-tree packing theorem of Hobbs, Bourgeois and Kasiraj (1987). In particular, the second tree is embedded without knowing the third, and the resulting pair of copies can be extended to accommodate every possible third tree.
Our strategy is to embed the first two trees so that their union is $2$-degenerate. We prove that the complement of every $2$-degenerate graph on $n$ vertices contains every tree of order $n-2$, which guarantees the final move. The main ingredient is an embedding lemma for spiders whose center must occupy a prescribed vertex having degree at most two in the forbidden graph. We then extend this lemma to arbitrary trees by induction.

papers.title: Glauber Dynamics for Sampling Colorings: Rapid Mixing above $(1+1/\mathrm{e})Δ$ via Hidden Hard-Core Models
papers.abstract: We show that for every $\gamma>0$ and every sufficiently large $\Delta$, the Glauber dynamics for proper $q$-colorings of any $n$-vertex graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has spectral gap $\Omega_\gamma(1/n)$, and hence mixing time $O_\gamma(n^2\log q)$, whenever $q\ge(1+1/\mathrm{e}+\gamma)\Delta$. Our proof establishes a Bochner-type inequality by exploiting the spectral gaps of hard-core models hidden in the color classes. The constant $1+1/\mathrm{e}\approx1.368$ comes from the uniqueness threshold $\approx\mathrm{e}/\Delta$ of the hard-core model on the infinite $\Delta$-regular tree.

papers.title: Fractional colorings of $K_r$-free graphs with local demands
papers.abstract:
We study fractional coloring with local demands, a framework introduced by Kelly and Postle in which one seeks a probability distribution on the independent sets of a graph such that each vertex $v$ is included with probability at least a prescribed target $\phi(v)$. For $K_r$-free graphs, Kelly and Postle conjectured that such a distribution exists provided $\phi(v)\le c_r\frac{\log d(v)}{d(v)}$ for a fixed \(c_r>0\), where $d(v)$ is the degree of $v$, and they established this up to a factor of $(\log\log d(v))^2$. In this paper, we prove their conjecture, showing that \[
\phi(v)\le\frac{c}{r}\frac{\log(d(v)+2)}{d(v)+1} \] suffices for an absolute constant $c>0$. As a corollary, we obtain a lower bound on the independence number of $K_r$-free graphs in terms of their degree sequence. This strengthens the bound that OpenAI proved in resolving the Ajtai-Erdős-Komlós-Szemerédi conjecture. Moreover, our argument yields a deterministic algorithm that produces the desired probability distribution in time $2^{O(r^2)}n^{O(1)}$, where \(n\) is the number of vertices and the implied constants are absolute.

papers.title: Two-block paths in oriented graphs under the Ore-type condition
papers.abstract:
Stein conjectured that for every positive integer $k$, every oriented graph with minimum semi-degree greater than $k/2$ contains every oriented path of length $k$ [Springer this http URL. 165 (2020), 459--486]. For directed paths this is a classical result of Jackson (1981). The two-block case of the conjecture was established by Chen, Hou and Zhou (2025). In this paper we prove the two-block analogue of Jackson's theorem.
For all positive integers $s$ and $r$, let $P(s,r)$ be the oriented path consisting of two directed paths of lengths $s$ and $r$ with a common terminal vertex, and let $Q(s,r)$ be its reverse. We show that for all $K\ge3$ and all $s,r\ge1$ with $s+r\le K$, every oriented graph $D$ with
$\delta(D)\ge K$ and $d_D^+(u)+d_D^-(v)\ge K-1$ for every ordered pair of distinct vertices
$(u,v)\notin A(D)$ contains both $P(s,r)$ and $Q(s,r)$. Our result is the two-block analogue of Jackson's theorem, and it extends the two-block result of Chen, Hou and Zhou. The proof iterates a shift of the terminal vertex of a longest path.

surveys.title: Lemmas and Conjectures in Spectral Graph Theory
surveys.abstract: The corpus of Elie Duhamel and Tristan Cazenave~\cite{dc} contains $305{,}755$ automatically generated conjectures relating spectral and metric invariants of connected graphs. A pipeline generated with Claude Code (numerical refutation, proof by the SMT solver \textsf{z3} from a library of lemmas, discovery of new lemmas, formalisation in \lean~4/Mathlib) refuted $162{,}964$ conjectures and proved $117{,}390$ without any unproved hypothesis, of which $79{,}505$ are verified end to end in \lean{} for every connected graph. This document collects, with proofs written for mathematicians, the most interesting lemmas that were discovered and proved, the ten most useful lemmas, the ten hardest theorems, simpler proofs of known results (Bollobás--Erdős, Yang--Lu), and the unrefuted conjectures that we find most interesting. All the proofs are gathered in an archive
